title: Za'atar Loin and Shoulder Lamb Board
displayTitle: Za'atar Loin and Shoulder Lamb Board
seoTitle: Za'atar Loin and Shoulder Lamb Board | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Mixed lamb chop board—two cuts, one platter, hall steakhouse energy
subtitle: Herb-rubbed loin and shoulder chops, rosemary board, and char for ten
description: Lamb loin and shoulder chops get rosemary-garlic rub, grill to 135°F, and arrange on a board with charred lemon, olives, and whipped feta.

steps.title: Rub lamb chops
steps.instruction: Combine rosemary, garlic, olive oil, lemon zest, and salt. Rub all chops and rest 1 hour at room temp. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use za'atar, sumac, pomegranate molasses, labneh as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Use pickled turnips, fresh mint, grilled pita wedges, Aleppo pepper as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Whip feta spread
steps.instruction: Blend feta with olive oil and lemon juice until smooth. Hold refrigerated until board assembly. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Heat grill zones
steps.instruction: Preheat grill with hot zone at 475°F and medium zone at 425°F. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill loin chops
steps.instruction: Grill loin chops over hot zone 3–4 minutes per side until 130°F internal. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill shoulder chops
steps.instruction: Grill shoulder chops over medium zone 5–6 minutes per side until 135°F internal. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Char lemons
steps.instruction: Grill lemon halves cut-side down 2 minutes at 450°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest all chops 5 minutes. Hold covered at 170°F in hotel pans until board assembly. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Board for ten
steps.instruction: Arrange mixed chops on board with whipped feta, olives, and charred lemon. Two chops per firefighter. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Cook loin and shoulder separately—they need different heat and time.
135°F pull with rest delivers pink loin and juicy shoulder.
Whipped feta at room temp spreads easier on the board.
tonightSpread: Mixed lamb chop board with whipped feta and olives.
Orzo salad with lemon and herbs.
leftovers: Slice leftover chops for lamb pita wraps.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Mixed chop boards feel special without slow cooking. Loin and shoulder eat differently on one board, hold sliced at 170°F, and beat another generic kebab platter.
mealPrepNotes: Rub chops 1 hour ahead. Grill loin hot 475°F, 3–4 minutes per side; shoulder medium 425°F, 5–6 minutes per side. Hold covered at 170°F up to 30 minutes.
